title: Variola virus
definition: A documented virus: Variola virus, family Poxviridae, Class I: dsDNA.
genome: Double-stranded DNA, linear, about 186,000 base pairs
structure: Large brick-shaped enveloped virion, roughly 300 x 240 x 100 nm; complex internal structure with lateral bodies; replicates in the cytoplasm
transmission: Respiratory droplets and prolonged close face-to-face contact; also via contaminated bedding and clothing
hosts: Humans only — no animal reservoir, which made eradication possible
discovered: Disease known since antiquity (described in ancient Egypt, India and China); the virus itself characterized in the early 20th century
history: Smallpox killed an estimated 300 million people in the 20th century alone. Edward Jenner's 1796 cowpox inoculation founded vaccination. medical_info: Causes smallpox (variola major, ~30% fatal; variola minor, milder). Documented countermeasure: live vaccinia-based smallpox vaccine. No specific antiviral cure was ever deployed at scale. General information only — not medical advice.

title: Vaccinia virus
definition: A documented virus: Vaccinia virus, family Poxviridae, Class I: dsDNA.
genome: Double-stranded DNA, linear, about 190,000 base pairs
structure: Brick-shaped enveloped virion similar to variola, about 300 nm long; cytoplasmic replication

medical_info: Documented use: the smallpox vaccine strain. It is the reference poxvirus for research. General information only — not medical advice.

title: Mpox virus

title: Varicella-zoster virus

title: Cytomegalovirus
